verdictReason: All Phase 5 invariants are proven by tests executing the real production code path (not reimplementations). Two P1 defects (canonical-authority bypass, page-context prompt injection) were found and fixed. Withheld from full CERTIFIED only because the fixes are not yet deployed to production.

defectsFound.description: System prompt told the model canonical facts were settled, but nothing enforced it; a hostile or weak model response passed straight through to the visitor.
context.route and context.entity were spliced unsanitized into the model prompt; any caller of the public API could forge a SYSTEM instruction or fake canonical-fact block.
Deterministic answer layer had no access to conversation history; every pronoun follow-up question fell through to a generic answer.
A rejected/failed mid-stream answer was appended to rather than replacing the already-streamed (possibly wrong or half-finished) text.
Several 'which project is for X' and 'which projects are public today' style questions fell through to a generic answer or the wrong entity.
0.82 similarity threshold let 'Forger' match 'forge' (CodeForge) and 'find' match 'finder' (FarmStand Finder).
'What is GEMS / Training Grounds?' incorrectly resolved to Peridot because 'Training Grounds' appeared in that lineage's own description text.

Focus was not returned to the composer after a turn; the conversation transcript rebuilt (and re-announced) on every message; toggle-open depended on rAF+setTimeout and could leave the panel non-interactive.
12000ms timeout was inherited without measurement; live sampling showed successes complete well under 8s while failures wasted the full 12s.

verifyAgainstCanon() is pattern-based, scoped to categories FDS's own data can adjudicate (version/availability/url/benchmark/cancellation/founder/metric/price); a subtly wrong relationship between two individually-correct facts would not be caught.
Retire residual knownAnswer() branches in src/data/kayla/index.ts now that canonicalAnswer() covers nearly everything they did.
Consider a quiet per-message source indicator now that settled answers never touch the model.
A manual (non-CI, non-automatic) live adversarial test against the real OpenRouter free-tier model would add confidence beyond the mocked-provider tests, but should not run automatically.
